Clinical Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck while turning left.
The reported mechanism, a direct impact with head movement during the turn, is consistent with the concussive
injury diagnosed at intake. Over the course of care, the patient attended 20 visits, a somewhat longer course than is
typical for an injruy of this type, with symptom management and graded activity adjusted as the patient progressed.
Examination findings support the diagnosis of concussion, including documented balance complaints, light sensitivity,
and reduced performance on certain cognitive screening items. Other neurological tests, including cranial nerve
assessment, strength, and reflexes, returned normal results. Imaging was not indicated based on the clinical
presentation.
The patient's medical history reveals no prior injury to the head or neck region. Billing records for the episode of care
reflect each service once, with no duplicated or repeated charges.
Current status: symptoms have improved but not fully resolved. Ongoing follow-up, graded return to activity, and
symptom monitoring are recommended.

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
